llm.summary: This looks like a scoped OpenClaw UI patch, but it needs review because it injects persistent browser code that polls and can reload the app despite also claiming no network access.

dimensions.detail: Browser-side MutationObserver, one-second heartbeat, localStorage size persistence, same-origin fetch('./', credentials:'same-origin'), and location.reload() are mostly purpose-aligned, but the network/reload behavior is under-disclosed relative to the 'no network' claims.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer auto-detects the OpenClaw Control UI directory, backs up index.html, injects one script tag, copies one versioned asset, and removes only matching older picker assets; this is high-impact local mutation but is disclosed and reversible with -Remove.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are mostly scoped to installing, verifying, repairing, and removing the OpenClaw Control UI patch; the broad natural-language trigger is install-oriented and not an agent override, but users should treat installation as an explicit action.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The injected script persists in the installed Control UI until uninstall or OpenClaw upgrade and stores UI size in localStorage; the ClawHub artifact does not include the scheduled watchdog, but documentation references an optional GitHub-only auto-repair task.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, a two-column OpenClaw model picker, matches the PowerShell installer and browser DOM enhancement, but the artifacts also include same-origin update polling with credentials and automatic reload behavior while some safety text says there is no network access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing if you are uncomfortable with a skill modifying your OpenClaw installation. Installing will patch index.html, add a browser script, hide the account row in the model menu, persist a picker size in localStorage, poll the same-origin Control UI page for updates, and sometimes reload the tab automatically. Use -Remove to uninstall, and prefer the ClawHub artifact if you do not want the GitHub-only scheduled repair watchdog.
llm.findings:
[RA1] expected: The self-update references describe a browser update checker and a GitHub-only repair watchdog; the ClawHub artifact did not contain the scheduled-task watchdog, and the included updater does not modify the skill files themselves.
[LP1] expected: The JavaScript does perform periodic same-origin fetch('./', {cache:'no-store', credentials:'same-origin'}) for update checks; this supports a review concern because other artifact text claims no network access.
[P2] unexpected: The flagged content was a UTF-8 BOM, Chinese comments, and an HTML marker regex; I did not find hidden agent instructions or prompt-injection directives in those locations.
[AE4] expected: The mixed-language README, sponsors, and documentation are consistent with the multilingual user-facing docs and did not show obfuscated commands, secrets, or evasive behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic reload is part of the documented self-updating behavior and includes loop and typing guards, but it is still a user-impacting action without explicit confirmation.
[SQP-1] expected: The natural-language install phrase is tied to OpenClaw Control UI installation and does not attempt to override agent behavior, though it is broader than a strict command-style trigger.
[SQP-3] expected: Fixed Chinese UI strings and multilingual/license-language choices are product-localization concerns, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The SARIF run reported no results; final concern comes from direct artifact inspection, not from a malicious static-scan finding.
